## Trump Account Calculator 2026 – Seed, $5,000 Limit & After-Tax Value
URL: https://j6-cloude.github.io/

Claiming is free. No one from the program will ask you for a fee to get the $1,000 or $250. Start from trumpaccounts.gov or irs.gov/trumpaccounts, not from a text, email or ad. What is a Trump Account? A Trump Account is an investing account for a U.S. child. A 2025 law created it (tax code section 530A). It works like a traditional IRA (a retirement account with tax rules) for a child under 18. Family and others can add up to $5,000 a year. Employers can give up to $2,500 of that. The money goes into low-cost U.S. stock index funds, with fees of 0.10% or less. In general, no one can take money out until the year the child turns 18. Children born 2025 to 2028 who are U.S. citizens can get a one-time $1,000 from the Treasury. Quick answer: at a 7% yearly return, the free $1,000 alone could grow to about $3,363 by age 18. Add $25 a month and it could be about $14,242. Add $1,000 a year and it could be about $39,627. Returns are not guaranteed. Frequently asked questionsWhat is a Trump Account?A Trump Account is an investing account for a U.S. child. A 2025 law created it (tax code section 530A). It works like a traditional IRA (a retirement account with tax rules) for a child under 18. Family and others can add up to $5,000 a year. Employers can give up to $2,500 of that. The money goes into low-cost U.S. stock index funds, with fees of 0.10% or less. In general, no one can take money out until the year the child turns 18. Children born 2025 to 2028 who are U.S. citizens can get a one-time $1,000 from the Treasury.How much will $1,000 in a Trump Account be worth at 18?At a 7% annual return (before a 0.03% fee), the $1,000 Treasury seed alone grows to about $3,363 by age 18. Returns are not guaranteed.What is the Trump Account contribution limit?$5,000 per child per year from family and others, of which up to $2,500 can come from an employer. The $1,000 Treasury seed, qualified government/charity contributions and rollovers do not count toward the limit. The limit is indexed to inflation after 2027.When can the money be withdrawn?Generally not before January 1 of the year the child turns 18. After that the account follows traditional IRA rules: earnings and pre-tax money are taxed as ordinary income when withdrawn, and withdrawals before age 59½ may face a 10% penalty unless an exception (such as qualified higher education or a first home) applies.SourcesIRS: Trump AccountsIRS: Trump Accounts – Frequently asked questionsIRS: Instructions for Form 454726 U.S.C. § 530A (statute text)Next stepCheck if my child qualifies &rarr;Takes 30 seconds. Details: the formula, the Dell $250 and taxes Each year until the child turns 18: balance = (balance + family + employer) × (1 + return − fee). The starting balance includes the $1,000 Treasury seed and/or the Dell $250 deposit if ticked. Dell $250: The Dell $250 went to eligible children born Jan 1, 2016 – Dec 31, 2024 living in ZIP codes with a median family income of $117,300 or less (U.S. Census 2020–2024 ACS), plus all eligible children on military bases; all deposits were made by October 9, 2026. It was automatic. Some children in higher-income ZIPs also got it because their families enrolled before auto-enrollment began; funds are reserved for children in foster care, expected next year. (Source: Invest America, figures as of Oct 9, 2026; verified Oct 27, 2026.) After-tax estimate. At 18 the account follows traditional IRA rules. Money the family put in was already taxed, so it is your basis (not taxed again). The seed, the Dell gift, employer money and all growth are taxed as income when taken out. The calculator applies your tax rate to that part and, if ticked, a 10% penalty before 59½. Real taxes depend on the year, your state and exceptions. Broad U.S. stock indexes have historically averaged roughly 10% nominal per year over long periods, with large losses in some years. ## Trump Account vs 529 Plan: Which Is Better for Your Child? (2026)
URL: https://j6-cloude.github.io/trump-account-vs-529/

Short answer: if college is the main goal, a 529 usually wins because qualified education withdrawals are tax-free, while Trump Account growth is taxed as income. Always grab the free $1,000 seed (and any employer money) first; then a 529 for education; a Trump Account makes more sense for long-term, non-education wealth. Trump Account vs 529: comparison table Trump Account (530A)529 plan Main purposeLong-term investing; becomes an IRA at 18Education (college, K-12 tuition up to limits, some apprenticeships) Free money$1,000 seed (born 2025–2028); possible Dell $250; employer up to $2,500/yr tax-free to employeeSome state matches/grants; no federal seed Annual limit$5,000 (plus exempt contributions)No annual federal limit; gifts above the annual gift-tax exclusion need reporting; high lifetime caps set by states Tax on contributionsNo federal deductionNo federal deduction; many states give a state deduction Tax on withdrawalsEarnings and non-basis money taxed as ordinary income; 10% penalty before 59½ unless an exception appliesTax-free for qualified education; earnings taxed + 10% penalty for non-qualified use InvestmentsOnly U.S. stock index funds, fees ≤ 0.10%, no leveragePlan menu: age-based, stock, bond, cash options AccessLocked until the year the child turns 18Any time (tax depends on use) Who controls it after 18The child (it becomes their IRA)The account owner (usually the parent) Which should you fund first? Elect the $1,000 seed on Form 4547 if your child was born 2025–2028 — it costs nothing. Take any employer Trump Account contribution; it is excluded from your income up to $2,500. For expected college costs, fund a 529 (check your state's deduction). Extra long-term money: a Trump Account, or a custodial Roth IRA if the child has earned income (see comparison). Run your own numbers in the Trump Account calculator, which estimates the tax due on withdrawal. Frequently asked questionsIs a Trump Account better than a 529?For college savings, a 529 is usually better because qualified education withdrawals are tax-free. A Trump Account is better for free money (the $1,000 seed, employer contributions) and long-term, non-education investing.Can I have both a Trump Account and a 529?Yes. Nothing prevents a child from having both.Can Trump Account money be used for college?After the account becomes IRA-like at 18, IRA rules apply: withdrawals for qualified higher-education expenses avoid the 10% early-withdrawal penalty, but the taxable part is still subject to income tax.SourcesIRS: Instructions for Form 454726 U.S.C. § 530A (statute text)IRS: Topic 557 – additional tax on early IRA distributions (exceptions)IRS: 529 plans – questions and answersNext stepRun your own numbers &rarr;See the value at 18 and what you keep after tax.

## Trump Account vs Custodial Roth IRA vs UTMA: Comparison Table
URL: https://j6-cloude.github.io/trump-account-vs-custodial-roth-ira/

Short answer: a custodial Roth IRA is the best tax deal (tax-free growth) but needs the child to have earned income. A Trump Account needs no earned income but growth is taxed on withdrawal. A UTMA/UGMA has no limits or investment restrictions but its earnings are taxed yearly (kiddie tax) and the child controls it at 18–21. Trump AccountCustodial Roth IRAUTMA/UGMA Child needs earned income?NoYes (contribution ≤ earned income)No Annual limit$5,000 (+ exempt contributions)IRA limit or child's earned income, whichever is lowerNone (gift-tax reporting above annual exclusion) Free money$1,000 seed (2025–2028 births), employer, charitiesNoneNone Tax on growthDeferred; taxed as income when withdrawnTax-free if qualifiedTaxed yearly (kiddie tax rules) InvestmentsU.S. stock index funds only, ≤0.10% feesAlmost anythingAlmost anything AccessFrom the year the child turns 18Contributions any time; earnings after 59½ (exceptions)Child takes control at state age of majority (18–21) Financial aidRules still developingRetirement assets generally not reported on FAFSACounted as the student's asset Use the calculator to see the after-tax difference at different tax rates. Frequently asked questionsIs a Roth IRA for kids better than a Trump Account?If your child has earned income, a custodial Roth IRA usually wins on taxes because qualified growth is tax-free. Many families can use both: the Trump Account for the free seed and non-earned money, the Roth for earned income.Does a Trump Account count against FAFSA?Federal guidance on how Trump Accounts are treated for financial aid is still developing; check studentaid.gov before relying on any assumption.SourcesIRS: Instructions for Form 4547IRS: Retirement topics – IRA contribution limitsNext stepRun your own numbers &rarr;See the value at 18 and what you keep after tax.

## How to Claim a Trump Account (Auto-Enrolled Since Oct 2026): Step by Step
URL: https://j6-cloude.github.io/how-to-claim-trump-account/

Short answer: since Oct 1, 2026, most kids under 18 with an SSN got an account opened for them. You claim it in the official Trump Accounts app or website. If your child was born 2025 to 2028, you also ask for the free $1,000 on Form 4547. It costs nothing. Never pay to claim. Scammers copy this program. Start from trumpaccounts.gov or irs.gov/trumpaccounts. Don't give an SSN to anyone who texts or calls you first. Step by step Get your details ready: your ID details, plus your child's legal name, SSN and date of birth, exactly as on their Social Security card. Open the official app or site: the Trump Accounts app (Apple App Store or Google Play), or the website linked from trumpaccounts.gov. Watch out for look-alike sites and texts. The SSA Inspector General warns about government imposter scams. Prove who you are and that you can manage the child's account. Claim and turn on the account. Ask for the $1,000 (U.S. citizen born 2025–2028): send Form 4547 and pick the pilot program contribution. You can do this in the app, on the website, or in your IRS Online Account. Optional: add money (up to $5,000 a year), and ask your employer if it adds money too. 🎉 Already claimed the $1,000? Celebrate it, and remind other parents to claim theirs. Nothing is checked or sent anywhere. I've claimed it — make my certificate Child's first name or nickname (optional) Download imageShare… FacebookText messageWhatsAppCopy link Link to share Just for fun: made by KidAccountMath, an independent site. Not a government document. Who runs it: Treasury picked BNY as financial agent. Robinhood Securities is the broker and first trustee (per the IRS FAQ). Help line: 866-USA-4547. Got a rejection? See Form 4547 / CP318 fixes. Frequently asked questionsIs Form 4547 required if my child was auto-enrolled?Not to open the account. You still need Form 4547 to request the $1,000 seed, and you must claim the account to manage it.Is Form 4547 a real IRS form?Yes. The IRS confirms Form 4547, Trump Account Election(s), is an official form.Who is the custodian of Trump Accounts?The IRS FAQ says Treasury designated BNY as financial agent and Robinhood Securities as brokerage provider and initial trustee.SourcesIRS: Trump AccountsIRS: Trump Accounts – Frequently asked questionstrumpaccounts.gov (official program site)SSA OIG scam alert on COLA/impostersNext stepCheck if the account is already open &rarr;How to look it up and spot fake apps and texts.

## IRS Notice CP318 / Form 4547 Rejected: What It Means and How to Fix It
URL: https://j6-cloude.github.io/form-4547-cp318-notice/

Short answer: Notice CP318 means the IRS could not complete or process your Trump Account election, most often because a name, SSN or date of birth does not match Social Security records. Fix the data and resubmit Form 4547 as the notice instructs. Do not file Form 1040-X. Common causes and fixes CauseWhat to check / do Child's name, SSN or DOB mismatchCompare with the Social Security card/record exactly (suffixes, hyphens, recent name changes). Resubmit Form 4547 per the notice. Your (responsible party's) details don't match IRS recordsUse the same legal name, SSN/ITIN and DOB as on your tax return. Account or election already existsAnother parent or guardian may already have elected; a child can have one funded Trump Account at a time. Claim the existing account in the app. Missing or unreadable informationCommon with forms filed alongside a tax return; resubmit electronically via the app, website or IRS Online Account. Child outside the age windowThe account must be established before the year the child turns 18. What not to do Don't file an amended return (1040-X) to fix Form 4547 — the IRS says not to. Don't expect IRS phone agents to correct the election; the IRS says they cannot. For account changes after claiming, the program line is 866-USA-4547. Don't give SSNs to anyone who contacts you first by text or phone. Frequently asked questionsWhy did I get Notice CP318?The IRS needs more action to complete or correct a Trump Account election, typically due to missing or mismatched information.Should I file Form 1040-X to fix Form 4547?No. The IRS says not to; follow the CP318 instructions and resubmit Form 4547.Can the IRS fix my election by phone?The IRS says its customer service representatives cannot correct the election by phone or help claim the account.SourcesIRS: Trump Accounts – Frequently asked questionsIRS: Instructions for Form 4547Next stepGo back to the claim steps &rarr;Fix the details, then resubmit Form 4547.

## How Do I Know If My Child Has a Trump Account? (Auto-Enrollment 2026)
URL: https://j6-cloude.github.io/does-my-child-have-a-trump-account/

Short answer: if your child has a valid SSN and is under 18, the Treasury has probably opened one automatically (auto-enrollment began October 1, 2026). To confirm, use the official Trump Accounts app or website: the IRS says you can check there whether an account has been established and then claim it. You may also get a Treasury letter if your child may qualify for the $1,000 contribution. How to check, step by step Install the Trump Accounts app from the Apple App Store or Google Play, or go to the website linked from trumpaccounts.gov. Verify your identity and your authority over the child. Enter the child's legal name, SSN and date of birth exactly as on Social Security records. If an account exists, you will be able to claim and activate it. Born 2025–2028? Separately elect the $1,000 seed (Form 4547) — auto-enrollment does not elect it for you. Born 2016–2024? Check whether the Dell $250 was deposited: it went automatically to kids in ZIP codes with median family income ≤ $117,300 or on military bases, all by Oct 9, 2026 (see the eligibility checker). (Source: Invest America, figures as of Oct 9, 2026; verified Oct 27, 2026.) Is the Trump Account app legit? The IRS's own Trump Accounts page tells parents to download the Trump Accounts app from the Apple App Store or Google Play to claim an account, and its FAQ names BNY as Treasury's financial agent and Robinhood Securities as brokerage provider and initial trustee. So the official app is real — but scammers imitate it. Safe habits: Start from irs.gov/trumpaccounts or trumpaccounts.gov, not from a text, email or ad link. No one from the program needs you to pay a fee to receive the $1,000 or $250. Don't give an SSN to anyone who contacts you first. The official help line is 866-USA-4547 (866-872-4547). Frequently asked questionsHow do I know if my child has a Trump Account?Use the official Trump Accounts app or website; the IRS says it lets you check whether an account was established for your child and begin claiming it. Since October 1, 2026 eligible children have been auto-enrolled.Is the Trump Account app legit?Yes, the IRS directs parents to the Trump Accounts app on the Apple App Store and Google Play. Reach it from irs.gov/trumpaccounts or trumpaccounts.gov to avoid imitations.Does auto-enrollment include the $1,000?No. You must still elect the $1,000 pilot contribution on Form 4547 if your child qualifies.Do I have to put money in?No. Contributions are optional; the account can hold just the seed or Dell gift.SourcesIRS: Trump AccountsIRS: Trump Accounts – Frequently asked questionstrumpaccounts.gov (official program site)Invest America: Dell $250 eligibility (figures as of Oct 9, 2026)Next stepClaim the account &rarr;The steps, in order, in the official app.

## Trump Account Rules 2026: Limits, Investments, Withdrawals and Taxes
URL: https://j6-cloude.github.io/trump-account-rules/

All the key Trump Account numbers in one place, with links to the IRS and the law. Words used here, in plain English Section 530A: the part of the federal tax code that created Trump Accounts. Traditional IRA: a retirement account. You pay income tax on growth when you take money out. Basis: money you put in that was already taxed. It is not taxed again when taken out. Index fund: one fund that holds many companies' stocks, like the S&amp;P 500. Rule2026 value Legal basisInternal Revenue Code § 530A (2025 tax law, signed July 4, 2025) Contributions allowed fromJuly 4, 2026 Automatic enrollmentEligible children auto-enrolled from October 1, 2026; parents must claim the account Annual limit (family, others, employer)$5,000 per child; indexed to inflation after 2027 Employer limit$2,500 per employee per year, excluded from the employee's income, counts toward $5,000 Exempt from the limit$1,000 Treasury seed, qualified general contributions (governments, 501(c)(3) charities), rollovers Treasury seed$1,000 one-time, U.S. citizens born Jan 1, 2025 – Dec 31, 2028, by election on Form 4547 Eligible investmentsMutual funds/ETFs tracking the S&amp;P 500 or another broad index of primarily U.S. companies; no leverage; fees ≤ 0.10%; no sector funds Growth period endsDecember 31 of the year before the child turns 18 WithdrawalsGenerally none before Jan 1 of the year the child turns 18 (exceptions: full rollover, certain ABLE rollovers, death); then traditional IRA rules Tax deduction for contributionsNone during the growth period BasisFamily/other contributions create basis (not taxed again); seed, charity, employer money and growth are taxable when withdrawn Dell $250 (private gift, not part of the law)Born 2016–2024, ZIP median family income ≤ $117,300 or on a military base; automatic; all deposited by Oct 9, 2026 (Source: Invest America, figures as of Oct 9, 2026; verified Oct 27, 2026.) Program operatorsBNY (financial agent), Robinhood Securities (brokerage/initial trustee), per IRS FAQ Frequently asked questionsCan a Trump Account invest in individual stocks or crypto?No. During the growth period it can only hold eligible mutual funds or ETFs tracking a broad U.S. equity index, with no leverage and fees of 0.10% or less.Do contributions to a Trump Account reduce my taxes?No federal deduction is allowed for contributions before the year the child turns 18. Employer contributions up to $2,500 are excluded from the employee's income.What happens at 18?The account generally becomes subject to traditional IRA rules and belongs to the child.Sources26 U.S.C. § 530A (statute text)IRS: Instructions for Form 4547IRS/Treasury guidance news releaseIRS: Trump Accounts – Frequently asked questionsInvest America: Dell $250 eligibility (figures as of Oct 9, 2026)Next stepCheck if my child qualifies &rarr;Turn the rules into a yes or no for your child.

## Trump Account Withdrawal Rules: What Happens at 18 (Tax Calculator)
URL: https://j6-cloude.github.io/trump-account-withdrawal-rules/

Short answer: no one can take money out before the year your child turns 18. Then the account turns into a normal traditional IRA in your child's name. Your child, not you, controls it. They can take money out, but part of it is taxed as income. Most withdrawals before age 59½ also owe a 10% extra tax. Some uses skip that 10%, like college costs or a first home (up to $10,000). Key facts Last year to add money: the year your child turns 17 (by Dec 31). From Jan 1 of the year they turn 18: IRA rules apply. At 18 your child signs in and takes control. You lose access. If no one ever claimed the account, it still becomes your child's IRA. The money is not lost. Withdrawal tax calculator Balance at 18 ($) Family money put in ($) Amount to take out ($) Child's income tax rate (%) Used for college costs or a first home (up to $10,000) or another IRS exception Child is 59½ or older The calculator needs JavaScript. See the worked example below. Worked example Say the account holds $25,000 at 18. Family put in $9,000 of their own (already-taxed) money. Your child takes out $5,000 for rent, at a 10% tax rate. AmountTax-free part (36% of the account is family money)$1,800Taxable part$3,200Income tax at 10%$32010% extra tax (rent is not an exception)$320Kept$4,360 If the same $5,000 paid for college, the 10% extra tax would not apply and your child would keep $4,680. The tax-free share follows the IRA pro-rata rule. A Trump Account is never combined with your child's other IRAs for this rule (Notice 2025-68). What can come out before 18? Almost nothing. During the growth period the law allows only these moves: A rollover of the whole balance to another Trump Account provider (trustee to trustee). A rollover to an ABLE account (for a child with a disability) in the year the child turns 17. Return of money put in over the $5,000 limit. Payment after the child's death. There is no hardship or emergency withdrawal before 18, unlike some other IRAs. Which uses skip the 10% extra tax after 18? The usual IRA exceptions apply. Common ones: qualified higher-education costs, up to $10,000 (lifetime) for a first home, and a few more listed by the IRS in Topic 557. Income tax still applies to the taxable part. See the full list at the IRS link below. What happens if my child leaves it alone? It keeps growing tax-deferred, like any IRA. After 18 your child can add more only under normal IRA rules, which need earned income (a job). Frequently asked questionsWhen can my child withdraw money from a Trump Account?Starting January 1 of the year the child turns 18. Before that, withdrawals are not allowed except for a full rollover, an ABLE rollover in the year the child turns 17, removing excess contributions, or death.Who controls a Trump Account at 18?The child. The account becomes a traditional IRA in their name; they set up their own login and the parent (responsible party) loses access.Is there a penalty for withdrawing from a Trump Account?After 18, the taxable part of a withdrawal before age 59½ generally owes a 10% additional tax unless an IRS exception applies, such as qualified higher-education costs or up to $10,000 for a first home. Income tax applies to the taxable part either way.Can you contribute to a Trump Account after 18?Not as a Trump Account. Contributions stop after December 31 of the year the child turns 17. After the account becomes a traditional IRA, the child can add money only under normal IRA rules, which require earned income.What happens if nobody claims the account?It stays invested. At 18 it converts to a traditional IRA in the child's name and the child verifies their identity to take control.SourcesTrump Accounts Help Center: overview and FAQTrump Accounts Help Center: contributions FAQTrump Accounts Help Center: claim an accountIRS Notice 2025-68 (Trump account guidance)Federal Register: Trump Accounts temporary regulations (Sept 30, 2026)IRS Topic 557: 10% additional tax on early IRA distributions (exceptions)26 U.S.C. § 530A (statute text)Next stepSee how each dollar is taxed &rarr;Which money is tax-free and which is taxed at 18.

## Are Trump Accounts Tax-Free? Deductions, Taxable Money and Tax Forms (2026)
URL: https://j6-cloude.github.io/trump-account-taxes/

Short answer: a Trump Account is tax-deferred, not tax-free. You get no tax deduction for what you put in. No one pays tax on the growth each year. When money comes out (age 18 or later), the growth is taxed as your child's income. The money family put in is not taxed again. Each kind of money, in one line Family money: no deduction going in; tax-free coming out. The $1,000 seed and charity gifts: taxed as income coming out. Employer money: not taxed to you going in (up to $2,500); taxed coming out. Growth: not taxed each year; taxed coming out. Tax treatment table Money sourceTax break going in?Tax-free coming out?Taxed as income when withdrawn?Family, friends, the childNoYes (basis)NoTreasury $1,000 seedn/aNoYesCharity or state gifts (qualified general contributions)n/aNoYesEmployer (§128, up to $2,500 per employee)Excluded from employee's income taxNoYesInvestment growthNot taxed yearlyNoYes Example: how much would be taxable at 18? Family addsValue at 18Tax-free (family basis)Taxable when withdrawn$0$3,363$0$3,363$50/month$25,121$10,800$14,321$100/month$46,880$21,600$25,280 Newborn with the $1,000 seed, 7% yearly return before a 0.03% fee, deposits at the start of each year until 17. Illustration only. Tax forms Form 5498-TA: sent each year for each account that got contributions. It is for your records; you generally do not file it. Form 1099-R: only if money comes out (for example, an excess contribution is returned). No 1099-DIV or 1099-INT. Dividends inside the account are not taxed each year, so there is no kiddie tax on them. Form 4547: the election form to open an account or get the $1,000. It is not a tax bill. Other tax points You cannot count a deposit made in early 2027 toward 2026. Every deposit counts for the calendar year it is made. Gifts from relatives can need a gift tax return only in rare cases. See grandparents and gift tax. Keep records of what family put in. That is the basis your child will not pay tax on later. Frequently asked questionsAre Trump Account contributions tax deductible?No. Personal contributions from parents, relatives or friends are not deductible. Employer contributions up to $2,500 per employee are excluded from the employee's income instead.Is a Trump Account tax-free?No. It is tax-deferred. Earnings are not taxed each year, but earnings, the $1,000 seed, employer money and charity gifts are taxed as ordinary income when withdrawn. Family contributions (basis) come out tax-free.What tax form do I get for a Trump Account?Form 5498-TA each year the account gets contributions, and Form 1099-R only if a permitted distribution is made. You generally do not need to file Form 5498-TA with your return.Do I have to report Trump Account earnings on my child's tax return each year?No. Earnings stay tax-deferred inside the account, and the account does not issue 1099-DIV or 1099-INT.Can I make a Trump Account contribution for last year?No. Contributions count toward the limit for the calendar year in which they are made.SourcesTrump Accounts Help Center: tax documents FAQTrump Accounts Help Center: investing FAQIRS Notice 2025-68 (Trump account guidance)IRS: Instructions for Form 454726 U.S.C. § 530A (statute text)Next stepEstimate tax on a withdrawal &rarr;Plug in a balance and see what you keep.

## Trump Account Rollover: Roth IRA, ABLE, 529 and Switching Providers
URL: https://j6-cloude.github.io/trump-account-rollover/

Short answer: before 18, you can only move the whole account to a new Trump Account firm. Or, in the year your child turns 17, to an ABLE account. You can't move it to a 529 or a Roth IRA. You can't move a 529 into it, either. At 18 it is a normal IRA. Then your child can move it to any IRA firm. They can also switch it to a Roth IRA and pay tax on the taxable part. What moves are allowed, by age MoveBefore 18 (growth period)From the year the child turns 18Move to another Trump Account providerYes, whole balance, trustee to trustee (when other providers exist)Yes (it is an IRA)Move to an ABLE accountOnly in the year the child turns 17IRA rulesMove to a 529 planNoNo direct rolloverConvert to a Roth IRANoYes; taxable part is taxed as incomeRoll to an IRA at Fidelity, Vanguard, Schwab etc.No (unless that firm becomes a Trump Account trustee)YesMove a 529, UTMA or custodial IRA into itNoNo (IRA rules apply to new money)Have two Trump Accounts with moneyNo; only one at a timen/a Can you switch away from Robinhood? Robinhood Securities is the first trustee. The rules allow a trustee-to-trustee move of the full balance to another approved Trump Account trustee. The official help center says this is available "when available," so for now there may be no other provider to move to. A move gives the account a new number; it does not reset any rules. Roth conversion after 18: tax estimate Converting moves money from the traditional IRA into a Roth IRA. Your child pays income tax now on the taxable part (seed, employer money, growth). After that, qualified Roth growth is tax-free. The family basis is not taxed again. Balance convertedFamily basisTaxable amountTax at 12%Tax at 22%$20,000$0$20,000$2,400$4,400$20,000$8,000$12,000$1,440$2,640$40,000$15,000$25,000$3,000$5,500 Simple estimate of federal tax on a full conversion. A low-income year (for example, a college year with little pay) means a lower rate. The 10% early-withdrawal tax does not apply to a direct conversion. Check current IRS rules or a tax pro before acting. Frequently asked questionsCan a Trump Account be converted to a Roth IRA?Not before 18. From the year the child turns 18 it follows traditional IRA rules, which include Roth conversions; the taxable part of the converted amount is taxed as ordinary income.Can I roll a Trump Account into a 529?No. The only rollovers allowed during the growth period are a full transfer to another Trump Account and an ABLE rollover in the year the child turns 17.Can I roll a 529 or custodial IRA into a Trump Account?No. The official help center says 529 plans and custodial IRAs cannot be rolled into a Trump Account, and ACATS transfers are not supported.Can I move my child's Trump Account to Fidelity or Vanguard?Only to another approved Trump Account trustee, and only the whole balance. After 18 it is a traditional IRA and can be moved to any IRA provider.Can my child have two Trump Accounts?Only one Trump Account with money in it at a time.SourcesIRS Notice 2025-68 (Trump account guidance)Federal Register: Trump Accounts temporary regulations (Sept 30, 2026)Trump Accounts Help Center: overview and FAQTrump Accounts Help Center: how to close or transfer an accountIRS: Instructions for Form 4547Next stepSee the rules at 18 &rarr;What changes the year your child turns 18.

## Can Grandparents Contribute to a Trump Account? How-To, Limits and Gift Tax
URL: https://j6-cloude.github.io/trump-account-grandparents/

Short answer: yes. Grandparents, aunts, uncles and friends can all add money. The parent who manages the account sends them a link or QR code from the app. They pay by bank account or debit card. Checks are not accepted. Everyone shares one limit: $5,000 per child per year in total. How a grandparent adds money The parent claims the account first. Gifts cannot go in before that. The parent opens the child's account in the app, taps the QR code icon, then Share link, and sends it by text or email. The grandparent opens the link and pays from a bank account or debit card. Bank transfers take up to 5 business days; debit cards are usually instant. Only the parent (the responsible party) can log in. Grandparents cannot see the balance in the app. Can a grandparent open the account? Sometimes. Form 4547 lists who may open an account: a legal guardian first, then a parent, then an adult sibling, then a grandparent. In most families the parent claims it. Only one person can manage it, and the first to finish the claim gets control. The $5,000 limit is shared If parents add $3,000 and a grandparent adds $2,500, the app declines anything past $5,000 for that year. Employer money also counts. The $1,000 Treasury seed and charity gifts do not count. What a monthly gift could grow to Grandparent givesStartingTotal given by 18Value at 18 (7%)$25/monthnewborn$5,400$10,879$25/monthage 5$3,900$6,451$50/monthnewborn$10,800$21,758$50/monthage 5$7,800$12,902$100/monthnewborn$21,600$43,517$100/monthage 5$15,600$25,803 7% yearly return before a 0.03% fee, deposits at the start of each year. Not guaranteed. Try your own numbers in the calculator. Gift tax: do grandparents need to file? Usually not. IRS Rev. Proc. 2026-25 gives a safe harbor. A cash gift to a Trump Account counts as a normal gift under the yearly exclusion ($19,000 per person in 2026) if all your gifts to that grandchild in the year stay at or under $19,000 and you do not otherwise have to file a gift tax return. If you give more than $19,000 to that grandchild in total, you file Form 709 and the Trump Account gifts must be reported too. Is it a good gift? It grows untaxed until 18, and the grandparent's money becomes basis, so it comes out tax-free later. The trade-offs: it is locked until 18, then the grandchild controls it. For college, a 529 may be better. See Trump Account vs 529 and FAFSA effects. Frequently asked questionsCan grandparents contribute to a Trump Account?Yes. Anyone can contribute once the account is claimed. The parent shares a contribution link or QR code from the app, and the grandparent pays by bank account or debit card.How much can a grandparent put in a Trump Account?All contributors together can add up to $5,000 per child per year (2026), including any employer money. Contributions over the limit are declined.Can grandparents open a Trump Account?A grandparent is on the list of authorized individuals in the Form 4547 instructions, after a legal guardian, parent and adult sibling. Only one person can be the responsible party.Do grandparents have to file a gift tax return?Generally no. Under Rev. Proc. 2026-25, cash Trump Account gifts are treated as present-interest gifts if the donor's total gifts to that grandchild for the year are no more than the $19,000 annual exclusion (2026) and no gift tax return is otherwise required.Can I mail a check to a Trump Account?No. The official help center says checks are not accepted; contributions are made electronically.SourcesTrump Accounts Help Center: make a contributionTrump Accounts Help Center: contributions FAQTrump Accounts Help Center: overview and FAQIRS: Instructions for Form 4547IRS Rev. Proc. 2026-25: gift tax safe harbor for Trump account contributionsIRS news release: safe harbor for certain Trump account contributionsNext stepSee what a monthly gift grows to &rarr;Try $25 or $50 a month from a grandparent.

## Trump Account Employer Contributions: $2,500 Rules and Companies Offering Them
URL: https://j6-cloude.github.io/trump-account-employer-contributions/

Short answer: an employer can put up to $2,500 a year into your children's Trump Accounts without it counting as income for you. The $2,500 is per worker, not per child. It counts toward each child's $5,000 limit. Over 50 companies have said they will offer it. Ask HR if yours does. The rules in plain words Limit: $2,500 per employee per year, in total for all your kids. It rises with inflation after 2027. Tax: left out of your federal income tax. Proposed IRS rules say it still counts as wages for Social Security and Medicare (FICA) tax unless another rule excludes it. Your own pay: an employer can let you put part of your pay in before tax through a cafeteria (Section 125) plan, but only for your dependent's account, not your own. Later: employer money is taxed as your child's income when withdrawn. It does not create basis. Plan needed: the employer must have a separate written plan, give notices and send yearly statements. Self-employed? Owners such as sole proprietors and partners can set up a plan for staff but cannot use it themselves (proposed rules). Companies that announced contributions Treasury's August 11, 2026 release quoted these companies: CompanyWhat Treasury's release saysVisaCompany match of the government's $1,000 contributionState StreetWill match the Treasury contributionFranklin TempletonMatching the government's contribution for eligible children of U.S. employeesVanguardCrew members can direct a $1,500 employer contribution to an eligible Trump AccountChimeEmployee match for Trump AccountsKrakenSponsoring a Trump Account for every child born in Wyoming in 2026ADP, Edward JonesSupportive statements; ADP plans payroll support for employer plans Details, start dates and eligibility vary; check your benefits portal. The official help center says employer contributions in the app are "coming soon." How much does it save? Employer puts inYour federal tax bracketFederal income tax you avoid$2,50012%$300$2,50022%$550$2,50024%$600 Compared with getting the same $2,500 as taxable pay. Federal income tax only; FICA still applies under the proposed rules. Your child pays tax later on withdrawal. If you have two kids The $2,500 cap covers both. The employer could put $1,250 in each, or $2,500 in one. Each child's own $5,000 cap still applies to everything added to that child. Frequently asked questionsHow much can an employer contribute to a Trump Account?Up to $2,500 per employee per year excluded from income, across all of the employee's children combined. It counts toward each child's $5,000 annual limit.Are employer Trump Account contributions taxable?They are excluded from the employee's federal income (up to $2,500). Proposed regulations say they are still wages for FICA and FUTA unless another exclusion applies. They are taxed to the child when withdrawn.Which companies match Trump Account contributions?Treasury's August 11, 2026 release cites Visa, State Street and Franklin Templeton matching the $1,000, Vanguard offering a $1,500 employer contribution, Chime offering a match, and Kraken sponsoring Wyoming babies born in 2026. Over 50 companies have committed.Can I contribute pre-tax from my paycheck?Yes, if your employer adds Trump Account contributions to its Section 125 cafeteria plan, for your dependent's account (not your own).Is the $2,500 per child?No. It is per employee, so two children share one $2,500 exclusion.Sources26 U.S.C. § 128 (employer contributions)IRS Notice 2025-68 (Trump account guidance)IRS news release: proposed regulations on employer contributions (Aug 11, 2026)Federal Register: proposed regulations under sections 128 and 129 (Aug 11, 2026)Treasury: employer contributions guidance and corporate commitments (Aug 11, 2026)Trump Accounts Help Center: tax documents FAQTrump Accounts Help Center: overview and FAQNext stepAdd employer money to the calculator &rarr;Open Advanced options and enter the employer amount.

## Does a Trump Account Affect FAFSA and Financial Aid? (2026)
URL: https://j6-cloude.github.io/trump-account-fafsa/

Short answer: no one knows yet. The U.S. Education Department has not said how to report a Trump Account on the FAFSA. FAFSA rules leave out retirement accounts like IRAs, and a Trump Account is legally a traditional IRA. So some experts think it will not count. Others think it will count as the student's money, which could cut need-based aid by up to 20% of the balance. Do not skip the free $1,000 over this. Even in the worst case, the aid you lose is smaller than the account itself. The two views ViewWhyWho says soNot reportedA Trump Account is a traditional IRA (IRC §408(a)). FAFSA instructions exclude retirement plans, including non-education IRAs.Kalman Chany (CNBC); Retirement Learning Center (PSCA, Oct 13, 2026)Reported as a student assetStudent assets are assessed at 20% in the Student Aid Index.Mark Kantrowitz (CNBC, Jul 9, 2026) Worst-case math Account balanceLost aid if a 20% student assetFor comparison: 5.64% (max rate on parent assets, e.g. a parent-owned 529)$2,500$500$141$6,000$1,200$338$10,000$2,000$564$25,000$5,000$1,410 Rates from CNBC's July 9, 2026 report. Only affects need-based aid. If FAFSA treats it like other IRAs, the asset effect is $0. Withdrawals can count as income Taxable money taken out in college counts as the student's income on a later FAFSA, which can reduce aid. One planning idea quoted by CNBC: wait to withdraw until Jan 1 of the student's sophomore year, so the income falls outside the years FAFSA looks at. Check this against current FAFSA rules before acting. What to do now Claim the account and the $1,000 if eligible. If college is the main goal for extra savings, a parent-owned 529 plan gets better aid and tax treatment. Watch studentaid.gov for Trump Account guidance. We will update this page when it appears. Frequently asked questionsDoes a Trump Account count on the FAFSA?Federal Student Aid has not issued guidance yet. Because a Trump Account is a traditional IRA, current FAFSA instructions excluding non-education IRAs suggest it may not be reported, but this is unconfirmed.How much financial aid could a Trump Account cost?If it were treated as a student investment asset, up to 20% of the balance per year in need-based aid (for example, up to $2,000 on a $10,000 account), according to Mark Kantrowitz via CNBC.Should I skip the $1,000 seed to protect financial aid?Experts quoted by CNBC say to claim it: in the worst case you would not lose more aid than the value of the account.Do Trump Account withdrawals affect financial aid?Taxable withdrawals add to the student's income, which can reduce aid on a later FAFSA.SourcesPSCA / Retirement Learning Center: Trump Accounts and FAFSA (Oct 13, 2026)CNBC: how Trump Account assets may affect college aid (Jul 9, 2026)IRS Notice 2025-68 (Trump account guidance)Federal Student Aid (studentaid.gov)Next stepCompare with a 529 plan &rarr;529s get better aid and tax treatment for college.

## What Is a Trump Account Invested In? SPYM, Fees and Historical Returns
URL: https://j6-cloude.github.io/trump-account-investment-options/

Short answer: right now all Trump Account money goes into one fund: SPYM, an S&amp;P 500 index fund. It holds about 500 large U.S. companies. You cannot pick another fund yet. The official help center says more choices are expected later. The fund fee is 0.02% a year (about $2 per $10,000). There is no account fee. The rules for what it can hold Only mutual funds or ETFs that track a broad index of mostly U.S. stocks (like the S&amp;P 500). No leverage. No single stocks, bonds, cash or crypto. Fund fees of 0.10% or less. Money is invested within about 1 business day. Dividends are reinvested. Is the money safe? It is held in a trust account by a registered trustee. SIPC covers up to $500,000 if the broker fails. SIPC does not cover market losses. The account can drop in value, and the government does not guarantee it. How much has $1,000 grown in the past? Treasury and the IRS looked at U.S. stock returns for children born 1926 to 2006. This is what $1,000 put in at each age was worth at 18: $1,000 added at ageBad case (10th percentile)Typical (median)Good case (90th percentile)At birth$2,980$6,180$13,8001$2,860$5,690$11,9902$2,680$4,920$10,0403$2,400$4,750$9,0304$2,150$4,260$8,0405$2,020$3,990$7,1106$1,770$3,620$6,3507$1,660$3,280$5,3808$1,680$3,150$4,6709$1,480$2,740$4,11010$1,350$2,460$3,56011$1,340$2,350$3,04012$1,180$2,050$2,72013$1,050$1,890$2,39014$1,020$1,630$2,06015$990$1,400$1,81016$970$1,240$1,59017$900$1,160$1,330 Source: Treasury and IRS, Table 3 in the temporary regulations (Sept 30, 2026). Based on a broad U.S. stock index for birth cohorts 1926 to 2006 (gross market returns, before fees). Past returns do not predict future returns. So for a newborn, the middle result was about 6 times the money. Even in a bad stretch (10th percentile) it nearly tripled. Money added at 17 had only one year, and in a bad year it lost value. What this means for you Earlier money matters most. $1,000 at birth did far better than $1,000 at age 10. You don't need to pick funds or time the market. There is one choice for now. If your child will need the money right at 18, remember the last year can be a down year. Frequently asked questionsWhat is a Trump Account invested in?All contributions are automatically invested in SPYM, an S&P 500 index ETF. There is no other option yet; more choices are expected for claimed accounts later.Can I choose investments in a Trump Account?Not at this time. By law, options are limited to low-cost, unleveraged funds tracking a broad index of mainly U.S. stocks.What are the fees on a Trump Account?No fee to claim or maintain the account. Funds may charge an expense ratio of at most 0.1%; SPYM's is 0.02%.Can a Trump Account lose money?Yes. It is invested in stocks and not guaranteed by the government. SIPC protection does not cover market losses.How much will $1,000 in a Trump Account be worth at 18?Treasury's historical data (birth cohorts 1926–2006) shows a median of about $6,180 for $1,000 invested at birth, with a 10th–90th percentile range of $2,980 to $13,800.SourcesTrump Accounts Help Center: investing FAQTrump Accounts Help Center: overview and FAQTrump Accounts Help Center: claim an accountFederal Register: Trump Accounts temporary regulations (Sept 30, 2026)IRS Notice 2025-68 (Trump account guidance)State Street: SPDR Portfolio S&P 500 ETF (SPYM) fact sheetNext stepRun your own growth numbers &rarr;Pick a return and see the value at 18.

Older kids do not get the $1,000 (that is only for U.S. citizens born 2025 to 2028). Many kids born 2016 to 2024 got $250 from the Dell gift. Starting late still helps, but there are fewer years to grow. ## Trump Account Pros and Cons: What's the Catch? (2026)
URL: https://j6-cloude.github.io/trump-account-pros-and-cons/

Short answer: it costs nothing to claim, and the $1,000 is free. So claim it. The catches come later. The money is locked until 18. Most of it is taxed when it comes out. At 18 your child gets full control. And for now there is just one fund. Pros Free money: $1,000 for U.S. citizens born 2025–2028. Possible employer, charity and state gifts. No fees to claim or keep it. The fund fee is 0.02% now (legal max 0.10%). No yearly tax on growth until money comes out. No earned income needed, unlike a custodial IRA. Simple: one low-cost S&amp;P 500 fund. Family money comes out tax-free (it is basis). The catches (cons) Locked until 18. No emergency withdrawals. Tax-deferred, not tax-free. Growth, the seed and employer money are taxed as income later. Many withdrawals before 59½ also owe 10%. Your child controls it at 18. You cannot stop them from spending it. No contribution deduction for family money. One fund only for now, all in U.S. stocks. It can fall in value. Can't be closed once claimed (except in rare cases). First to claim wins. Between separated parents, whoever finishes the claim first manages it. FAFSA effect is unknown (see FAFSA guide). Scams copy the program. Real notices come only from the official app, trumpaccount.com, or no-reply@trumpaccounts.treasury.gov. Which account wins for which goal? GoalUsually bestClaim the free $1,000 / employer moneyTrump AccountSave for college529 plan (tax-free for school, better for aid)Teen has a jobCustodial Roth IRA (tax-free growth)Money the child may need before 18Savings or UTMA accountLong-term gift with no earned incomeTrump Account Does it really grow? Treasury's own history check: $1,000 put in at birth in a broad U.S. stock index was worth $6,180 at 18 in the middle case and $2,980 in a bad (10th percentile) case, for children born 1926–2006. See investment options. Frequently asked questionsWhat's the catch with Trump Accounts?The money is locked until 18, most of it (growth, seed, employer money) is taxed as income when withdrawn, the child controls it at 18, there is only one fund for now, and the financial aid treatment is not yet settled.Is a Trump Account worth it?Claiming is free and the $1,000 seed (for eligible children) is free money, so claiming is generally worth it. Whether to add your own money depends on your goal: 529s are usually better for college and custodial Roth IRAs for teens with jobs.Are there fees on Trump Accounts?There is no fee to claim or maintain the account. Funds may charge up to 0.1%; the current fund, SPYM, charges 0.02%.Can I close a Trump Account?Once claimed it generally cannot be closed until 18, except in limited cases such as the child's death or an ABLE rollover.Is the Trump Account a scam?No, the program is real and run under IRS and Treasury rules, but scammers imitate it. Real activation emails come only from no-reply@trumpaccounts.treasury.gov.SourcesTrump Accounts Help Center: overview and FAQTrump Accounts Help Center: claim an accountTrump Accounts Help Center: investing FAQIRS Notice 2025-68 (Trump account guidance)Federal Register: Trump Accounts temporary regulations (Sept 30, 2026)CNBC: how Trump Account assets may affect college aid (Jul 9, 2026)Next stepClaim the account (free) &rarr;Step by step, in the official app.

## Trump Account App Problems: Can't Verify Identity, Login and 'Unable to Process' Fixes
URL: https://j6-cloude.github.io/trump-account-app-problems/

Short answer: most claim errors come from a mismatch. The name, SSN or birth date you typed must match what the IRS and Social Security have on file, for you and your child. Fix it in your IRS online account, then send a new claim form. You need a photo ID and a live selfie to verify. Delays of a few days can be normal. Stay safe. The real app is "Trump Accounts" on the Apple App Store or Google Play, or trumpaccount.com. Activation emails come only from no-reply@trumpaccounts.treasury.gov. No one will ask for your password or a one-time code. Fixes by error message ProblemWhat to doCan't verify my identityHave a valid government photo ID and good light for the live selfie. Use your legal name, SSN or ITIN and birth date exactly as on your tax return. If verification fails as the responsible party, sign in to your IRS online account, correct your election details, and submit a new claim form.My child is ineligible / can't be verifiedUsually the child's name, SSN or birth date doesn't match your tax return or Social Security records. In your IRS online account go to My Elections, then Unable to Process, read the notice, correct it, and resubmit.Child already has an accountOnly one account per child. Another parent or guardian may have claimed it first. The help center can't share who (tax privacy law). Talk to the co-parent, or contact support if you think it was not authorized.Status says ProcessingWait for the email from no-reply@trumpaccounts.treasury.gov. IRS processing usually takes 1–3 business days.Child turns 18 this yearToo late: the account must be opened before the year the child turns 18. This can't be overridden.No SSN yet (newborn or parent)The child needs an SSN; you need an SSN or ITIN. Submit the claim form once you have them.Forgot to elect the $1,000Not too late. Submit a new claim form with the pilot program election.Started but didn't finishYour claim progress is saved. Sign back in with the same username and password. (The paper-style Form 4547 screens are not saved if you close before identity verification.)Deposit reversed or card declinedMake sure the bank account has enough money; you get an email if a deposit is reversed, and many reversals can unlink the bank. A debit card must allow online purchases. Check your claim status Sign in to your IRS online account with ID.me. Go to Forms, then Trump Accounts. Read the Election status table. "Unable to process" links to a notice that says why (see CP318 guide). App basics Works on iOS 16 or newer, Android 7 or newer, and Chrome, Safari, Firefox and Edge. Tablets may work but are not officially supported. Only the responsible party can log in. There is no shared login yet. One login can manage several children: use Add child in the account switcher. Help line: 866-USA-4547 (866-872-4547), as listed on IRS.gov/trumpaccounts. Or use the support pages in the app. Frequently asked questionsWhy can't the Trump Account app verify my identity?The most common cause is a mismatch between what you entered (legal name, SSN or ITIN, date of birth) and IRS records. Correct your election in your IRS online account and submit a new claim form. Verification needs a government photo ID and a live selfie.Why does it say my child already has an account?Each child can have only one Trump Account, and the first eligible adult to complete the claim becomes the responsible party. Another parent or guardian may have claimed it.How long does the Trump Account claim take?The official help center says IRS processing of the claim form takes 1–3 business days; you then get an email from no-reply@trumpaccounts.treasury.gov to finish claiming.Is there a deadline to claim the Trump Account?No. Unclaimed accounts stay open and invested and become the child's traditional IRA at 18.Can both parents log in?No. Only the responsible party can log in for now; read-only access for a trusted contact is planned.SourcesTrump Accounts Help Center: complete the claim form (Form 4547) and 'unable to process'Trump Accounts Help Center: claim an accountTrump Accounts Help Center: overview and FAQTrump Accounts Help Center: contributions FAQIRS: Trump Accounts – Frequently asked questionsNext stepFix a CP318 notice &rarr;What the IRS letter means and how to resubmit.

## Trump Account Deadlines and Key Dates (2025–2029): Is There a Deadline to Claim?
URL: https://j6-cloude.github.io/trump-account-deadlines/

Short answer: there is no deadline to claim your child's account. The real cut-offs are about age: the account must be set up before the year your child turns 18, and deposits stop after Dec 31 of the year they turn 17. The $1,000 is for babies born from Jan 1, 2025 to Dec 31, 2028. You can elect it any time. Proc. 2026-25)Jul 4, 2026Contributions open; app launchesAug 11, 2026Employer contribution rules proposed; 50+ companies commitSep 30, 2026Temporary regulations publishedOct 1, 2026Treasury starts opening accounts automatically for eligible childrenOct 9, 2026Dell $250 deposits completedAfter 2027$5,000 and $2,500 limits start rising with inflationDec 31, 2028Last birth date that qualifies for the $1,000 "Deadline June 30" searches refer to the date the IRS added online Form 4547 filing in 2026, not a deadline to sign up. Frequently asked questionsIs there a deadline to sign up for a Trump Account?No deadline to claim an account that was opened for your child. An account must be set up before the year the child turns 18.Is there a deadline for the $1,000 Trump Account money?No fixed filing deadline was announced; the official help center says you can elect it any time. The child must be a U.S. citizen born January 1, 2025 through December 31, 2028.What was the June 30 Trump Account date?June 30, 2026 is when the IRS let people file Form 4547 through their IRS online account and announced gift-tax relief. It was not a sign-up deadline.When do Trump Account contributions stop?After December 31 of the year the child turns 17.When did automatic enrollment start?Treasury began opening accounts automatically for eligible children on October 1, 2026. Parents still need to claim them.SourcesTrump Accounts Help Center: claim an accountTrump Accounts Help Center: complete the claim form (Form 4547) and 'unable to process'IRS Notice 2025-68 (Trump account guidance)Federal Register: Trump Accounts temporary regulations (Sept 30, 2026)IRS/Treasury guidance news releaseIRS news release: safe harbor for certain Trump account contributionsTreasury: employer contributions guidance and corporate commitments (Aug 11, 2026)Invest America: Dell $250 eligibility (figures as of Oct 9, 2026)Next stepCheck if my child qualifies &rarr;Takes 30 seconds.
